paper_metadata.title: Composition design and microstructure of Ni-based single crystal superalloy with low specific weight—numerical modeling and experimental validation

evidence.quote: Ni‑based single crystal (SX) superalloys with low specific weight are essential for developing aero engine turbine blades with great strength to weight ratios.

To develop Ni-based SX superalloys with low specific weight, numerical analysis models for specific weight, the volume fraction of γ′ phase and elemental partitioning coefficients between γ and γ′ phases are collected and analyzed based on literature data.
The specific weight of model alloys is below 8.4 g/cm3, which all exhibit typical γ/γ′ two phase structure of Ni-based SX superalloy

evidence.quote: Ingots were prepared by arc melting pure Ni, Co, Mo, Re, Ti, Ta, Al, and Cr (purity > 99.9 wt%) in an argon atmosphere.

other.product: round rods 12.5 mm diameter, 120 mm length

evidence.quote: The arc melted alloys were then drop cast into a water chilled copper mold to produce round rods with 12.5 mm in diameter and 120 mm in length.
the as cast rods were solid solution treated in a stepwise process [1290 °C/2 h + 1305 °C/2 h + 1320 °C/4 h/air cooling (AC)] to eliminate the compositional/microstructural inhomogeneities
and then aged by two step process (1080 °C/4 h/AC + 870 °C/20 h/AC) to obtain the typical well defined γ/γ′ two phase microstructures. All heat treatments were carried out in argon.
